Calculate Extended Silhouette Width for Multi-Way Clustering

Source: R/extSilhouette.R
extSilhouette.Rd

Computes an extended silhouette width for multi-way clustering (e.g., biclustering, triclustering, or n-mode tensor clustering) by combining silhouette widths from a list of Silhouette objects, each representing one mode of clustering. The extended silhouette width is a weighted average of the average silhouette widths of the modes. By default each mode is weighted by its number of objects; equal or user-specified weights are also available. The output is an object of class extSilhouette.

Usage

extSilhouette(
  sil_list,
  dim_names = NULL,
  print.summary = FALSE,
  weights = c("size", "equal")
)

# S3 method for class 'extSilhouette'
format(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'extSilhouette'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

sil_list

A list of objects of class "Silhouette", typically the output of Silhouette or softSilhouette, where each object represents the silhouette analysis for one mode of multi-way clustering (e.g., rows, columns, or other dimensions in biclustering or tensor clustering).

dim_names

An optional character vector of dimension names (e.g., c("Rows", "Columns")). If NULL, defaults to "Mode 1", "Mode 2", etc.

print.summary

Logical; if TRUE, reports the extended silhouette width and the dimension table through message. Default is FALSE.

weights

How the modes are weighted: "size" (the default) weights each mode by its number of objects, "equal" gives every mode the same weight, and a non-negative numeric vector with one entry per mode gives user-specified weights (they are rescaled to sum to 1).

x

An object of class "extSilhouette".

digits

Number of decimal places shown.

...

Further arguments, currently ignored.

Value

A list of class "extSilhouette" with the following components:

ext_sil_width

A numeric scalar, the extended silhouette width.

dim_table

A data frame with columns dimension (e.g., "Mode 1", "Mode 2"), n_obs (number of objects), weight (the share of the total weight given to the mode) and avg_sil_width (average silhouette width of the mode).

weights

The weighting used: "size", "equal" or "user".

Values are not rounded; the print method shows four decimals.

Details

The extended silhouette width is computed as: $$ ExS = \frac{ \sum_{i} \omega_i \bar{S}_i }{ \sum_{i} \omega_i } $$ where \(\bar{S}_i\) is the average silhouette width of mode \(i\) (from summary(x)$avg.width, so it follows the averaging rule of that object) and \(\omega_i\) is its weight. With weights = "size", \(\omega_i = n_i\), the number of objects in mode \(i\) (nrow(x)), as in Schepers et al. (2008); ExS is then the average width over all objects of all modes, each object counting once. With weights = "equal", \(\omega_i = 1\), so ExS is the mean of the mode-wise averages.

Size weighting treats every clustered object alike, but when the modes differ greatly in size the largest mode dominates: with 200 rows and 30 columns, the rows receive about 87\ of the weight. Equal weighting gives every mode the same say regardless of its size. Because the choice can change which model is selected, report the mode-wise averages in dim_table together with ExS.

Each Silhouette object in sil_list must contain at least one observation and have a finite average width. For consistency, compute all Silhouette objects with the same function, method and averaging rule.

References

Schepers, J., Ceulemans, E., & Van Mechelen, I. (2008). Selecting among multi-mode partitioning models of different complexities: A comparison of four model selection criteria. Journal of Classification, 25(1), 67–85. doi:10.1007/s00357-008-9005-9

Bhat Kapu, S., & Kiruthika, C. (2025). Block Probabilistic Distance Clustering: A Unified Framework and Evaluation. PREPRINT (Version 1) available at Research Square. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-6973596/v1

See also

Silhouette, softSilhouette, dbSilhouette, cerSilhouette, getSilhouette, is.Silhouette

Examples

# Two modes: 150 objects in 3 clusters and 4 variables in 2 clusters
set.seed(123)
prob_mode1 <- matrix(runif(150 * 3), nrow = 150, ncol = 3)
prob_mode1 <- prob_mode1 / rowSums(prob_mode1)
prob_mode2 <- matrix(runif(4 * 2), nrow = 4, ncol = 2)
prob_mode2 <- prob_mode2 / rowSums(prob_mode2)

sil_mode1 <- softSilhouette(prob_matrix = prob_mode1, method = "pac")
sil_mode2 <- softSilhouette(prob_matrix = prob_mode2, method = "pac")

# Size-weighted (default) and equally weighted extended silhouette
extSilhouette(list(sil_mode1, sil_mode2), dim_names = c("Rows", "Columns"))
#> ------------------------------------------
#> Extended silhouette (size weights): 0.2202
#> ------------------------------------------
#> Dimension summary:
#>  dimension n_obs weight avg_sil_width
#>       Rows   150  0.974        0.2113
#>    Columns     4  0.026        0.5530
extSilhouette(list(sil_mode1, sil_mode2), dim_names = c("Rows", "Columns"),
              weights = "equal")
#> -------------------------------------------
#> Extended silhouette (equal weights): 0.3822
#> -------------------------------------------
#> Dimension summary:
#>  dimension n_obs weight avg_sil_width
#>       Rows   150    0.5        0.2113
#>    Columns     4    0.5        0.5530
